hypotheses.observation: In the dated search probe the signed exact page appeared at rank 30 for KAIST and rank 17 for Aalto. This is a candidate-list result, not proof that the production pipeline fetched either page. The older HTTP-only capture failed before returning either exact programme. 2026-09-27: the Aalto exact page surfaced at search rank 4 for the blind expert, but www.aalto.fi robots.txt timed out from GitHub runners 3/3, so headroom is blocked at access, not ranking.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: Reserve a bounded exploration share for high-value official candidates below the ordinary confirmation cutoff, using distinct host/page-kind signals and preserving the ranked top set.
hypotheses.integration_seam: backend/app/adapters/search/retrieval.py and backend/app/adapters/discovery/live_discovery.py; evaluate selection before changing either
hypotheses.counterexample: Opening rank 30 on every university can exhaust the same fetch budget and lower decision-grade precision; a low-ranked page can also be the wrong programme.
hypotheses.falsification: On a frozen candidate set and equal total Fetcher budget, compare exact programme recall@fetch-budget and pages-to-first-gold. Reject if the proposed reserve displaces a correct top candidate, fails on held-out universities, or adds a wrong-scope accepted claim.
hypotheses.policy_guard: All page reads through Fetcher; robots, egress, rate limits, identity and scope checks remain binding.

hypotheses.observation: The probe's Toronto exact page is rank 4 while the top candidate still has identity needs_review. The project review documents wrong-campus results under the same registrable domain. The signed Toronto case names St George, but the public request does not name a campus. 2026-09-27 blind trace (runs.2026-09-27/toronto.trace.json): with www/future.utoronto.ca answering 403, the expert reached www.utsc.utoronto.ca and proved six verbatim Scarborough facts; the official programme page lists Mississauga, Scarborough and St. George, so none answers the St. George label. Direct support for keeping campus unresolved; still untested as a rule. 2026-09-28: 2026-09-28 owner: implement the recommendation. Registry `campuses` (verified hosts; Toronto only: Mississauga, Scarborough) + app/domain/campus.py; runner verify stage withholds campus-specific claims when the request names no campus and adds one non-blocking 'campus' question. Funding stage not yet covered. Default on (correctness rule, not a discovery switch); live effect to be measured on the next benchmark: toronto precision must not fall, exact programme recall must not fall. Status stays candidate until the live measurement.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: Keep campus as an explicit unresolved identity dimension when official sources describe distinct application routes; do not treat same university domain or a strong seed-host score as campus proof.
hypotheses.integration_seam: backend/app/adapters/search/identity.py and backend/app/domain/programme_identity.py after a separate entity-contract design decision
hypotheses.counterexample: Some universities use campus names only as locations for one common programme; inventing campus separation from hostname alone would reject a valid route.
hypotheses.falsification: On human-adjudicated multi-campus and single-route cases, verify that unresolved requests abstain, named-campus requests choose only matching evidence, and exact programme recall does not fall. A same-domain rule alone is insufficient.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Verified registry and official page evidence may establish campus relationships; snippets and hostname similarity are discovery hints only.

hypotheses.observation: Search now surfaces exact programme pages for these three cases in a probe, while the only committed ten-case end-to-end claim capture predates the search and scope work. The current search insertion path appends results as programme-page candidates. No current end-to-end claim recovery is measured.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: After programme identity is established, create separate unresolved evidence obligations for admissions, country qualification, year-specific costs and scholarships; route candidate pages by obligation without treating a page-kind hint as final evidence.
hypotheses.integration_seam: backend/app/adapters/discovery/live_discovery.py category routing and an evaluation-only oracle-URL experiment before any production scheduler
hypotheses.counterexample: A general admissions page may contain valid programme-wide English rules; a hard programme-only category can discard it. One page can satisfy several obligations, and absence of a rule cannot prove a negative claim.
hypotheses.falsification: Run a fresh bounded end-to-end capture and an oracle-URL replay. Reject if obligation routing does not raise correctly scoped claim recall under the same budget, or if it increases unsupported or wrong-year accepted claims.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Official fetched excerpt plus programme, applicant and year scope remain mandatory; UNKNOWN remains a valid outcome.

hypotheses.observation: Toronto baseline 2026-09-27: all three programme slots went to future.utoronto.ca after that host had answered 403 to every read in the same run.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: A search candidate on a host that already refused this run's Fetcher outright (401/403, unreadable robots.txt, stalled) takes no programme-page slot.
hypotheses.counterexample: Freed slots go to the next ranked candidates, which may be worse than nothing.
hypotheses.falsification: ABBA paired captures on one runner, equal 60-call/120 s budget, 3 development and 9 held-out universities; reject if claims or verified claims do not rise or identity of chosen pages degrades.
hypotheses.policy_guard: All reads via Fetcher; robots and 403 are respected, never bypassed.

hypotheses.observation: Blind KAIST trace: the '학부 입학' (undergraduate admission) navigation link on every cs.kaist.ac.kr page read by the baseline was never opened; opening it recovered the signed programme.admission_route fact at 13/60 calls. Tested 2026-09-27 (3962468, cloud runners, ABBA, 60 calls/120 s, 3 dev + 9 held-out): the process metric failed - no arm opened cs.kaist.ac.kr/content?menu=40, because hop candidates are appended after search results and the three programme slots fill first. Claim differences are not the rule's: Vilnius on 3/off 0 follows Serper ranking the Bioinformatics page 2nd vs 3rd, and those 3 'verified' claims are for Bioinformatics, not the requested computer science (wrong programme); NU completed in one arm only (network). Also: no extractor emits ADMISSION_ROUTE, so even reaching the page could not add a claim. Rejected in this form; a retry needs a slot for navigation evidence and an extractor.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: Before score-based ranking, promote same-site navigation links whose anchor text matches an admissions/degree-level lexicon in the site's language.
hypotheses.integration_seam: backend/app/adapters/discovery/live_discovery.py navigation fallback and catalog walker lead scoring
hypotheses.counterexample: Admission menus are often generic institution pages that consume slots without programme evidence; lexicons per language can overfit.
hypotheses.falsification: ABBA paired captures on development and held-out universities (incl. non-English sites) at equal budget; reject if verified claims do not rise or wrong-scope claims appear.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Anchor text is a discovery hint only; claims still need fetched verbatim evidence and scope.

hypotheses.observation: KAIST baseline and ER-04 captures chose ftp.kaist.ac.kr (CTAN PDF), pure.kaist.ac.kr (clipping) and an.kaist.ac.kr/courses/2006 as programme pages; held-out Vilnius chose infedu.vu.lt journal pages and Tartu a conference news item. Tested 2026-09-27 (1134da3, cloud runners, ABBA, 60 calls/120 s): the switch removed the ftp/pure/2006-archive pages from KAIST's slots and a journal article from Vilnius's, but verified claims were equal in every paired arm on all 12 universities (Charles 3/3, Tartu 2/2, Vilnius 3/3, TUM 1 vs off 1/0, others 0). No precision or scope loss, no recall gain: neutral. Not promoted; switch stays off. Its value depends on a later extraction step (KAIST's freed slots went to bcs.kaist.ac.kr and the admissions index, which yielded no claims).
hypotheses.proposed_rule: Mirror, repository, research-portal, journal and dated course-archive hosts/paths are not programme-page candidates.
hypotheses.counterexample: Some universities host real programme pages under unusual subdomains; a host-name list can reject a valid route.
hypotheses.falsification: Paired captures at equal budget; reject if a correct programme page is lost on any case or verified claims fall.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Rejection only removes discovery candidates; no evidence rule is relaxed.

hypotheses.observation: ER-05 showed navigation-hop candidates never reach a programme slot, so KAIST's '학부 입학' page (where the new ADMISSION_ROUTE reader works: oracle 8 -> 9 facts) is never opened end to end. Tested 2026-09-27 (8b68958): claims equal in every pair on all 12 universities. KAIST produced no hop candidate at all (cloud runner read 7-9 pages instead of ~25), so the slot never applied there. Elsewhere the slot went to web.cs.utoronto.ca/bachelor-of-computer-science (plausible, no claims), iro.sabanciuniv.edu application requirements, but also to a Vilnius journal article, TUM research/Pure person pages and Tartu master-thesis pages. Rejected.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: Keep one of the three programme-page slots for the best navigation-hop candidate; search fills the other two.
hypotheses.counterexample: The best hop candidate is often a research, thesis or journal page; giving it a slot displaces a search result that may be the programme.
hypotheses.falsification: ABBA paired captures on one runner, equal 60 calls/120 s, admission lexicon on in BOTH arms, 3 development + 9 held-out; reject if KAIST menu=40 is not read or claims do not rise, or if wrong-programme pages take the slot.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Reads via Fetcher only; slot changes discovery order, never evidence rules.

hypotheses.observation: 2026-10-04 expert traces (claude-opus-5, not blind: gold seen earlier in session): Groningen, NTU and HKU publish the English minimum, the international fee and the deadline on topic pages the requirements adapter never opens (it reads program.url + admissions_url only); one Exa query per topic ranked that page first among the institution's results. Paired run 37234751647 (off/on x2, 120 s / 60 reads, exa): NTU core questions 2/6 -> 4/6 in both on arms (IELTS 6.5, subscores 6.5, TOEFL 90 correct); one wrong value: admission_deadline 2026-10-15 is the application window start (window 15 Oct 2026 - 20 Jan 2027) read by the existing deadline extractor from the newly reached important-dates page. Groningen times out before a programme page is known in both arms (ER-08 needs program.url); HKU robots-unreachable from runners; UBC page budget; Vienna unchanged. No other regression. Re-pair 37237138067 (after the window-start fix, 7 cases off/on x2): NTU deadline now abstains and IELTS 6.5/subscores/TOEFL 90 stay; Delft gains TOEFL iBT 90 (correct, bsc-international-diploma admission page); UBC gains intake.open (Nov 15 2026 apply page); one new wrong value: NTU intake 'spring 2026' read from the end of an application window ('... to 19 March 2026') - fixed by a range guard in extract_intake_terms. Groningen/HKU/Vienna/Warsaw unchanged; no lost values.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: After a programme page is known, send one public query per topic (English requirements, international tuition, application deadline) restricted to the institution domain; read the first same-institution result outside excluded paths and other degree levels; read tuition tables on programme and fee pages.
hypotheses.counterexample: A date-range or multi-qualification page (NTU important dates) makes the existing deadline extractor take a window start for the deadline.
hypotheses.falsification: Enable only if a paired run shows more correct core answers with no new wrong value; fix the date-range deadline reading first and re-run the pair.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Only the institution name enters a query; pages are read through the Fetcher with robots and official-domain checks; snippets never become facts.

hypotheses.observation: 2026-10-04 Groningen discovery read order (run 37234751647): publicSitemap-00001.xml is too_large, the navigation fallback reads /education/bachelor and takes brochures, open-day, campus-tour, webklassen and nederlandse-studenten pages as programme leads on URL structure alone; confirm and walker spend ~20 reads rejecting them and the wall clock ends before /bachelors/computing-science (which states deadline 1 May 2027 non-EU and fee EUR 19,800 non-EU 2027-28).
hypotheses.proposed_rule: When the applicant named a subject, the navigation fallback keeps a programme-page lead only if its URL or its link text names that subject (strong aliases included); catalogue-shaped links are still followed.
hypotheses.counterexample: A programme linked under an opaque URL and a label that is not the subject's name (e.g. a faculty brand name) would be dropped from navigation; the catalogue walker still reads it.
hypotheses.falsification: Enable only if a paired run reaches the Groningen programme page within budget with no lost programme page on the other cases.
hypotheses.policy_guard: Fewer reads, no new sources; nothing is read that the fallback would not have read.
